question: On unpatched Hermes Agent with the DGX route, how do the warm_compaction plugin, hermes-lcm, and the built-in compressor compare in compaction speed and in what the agent still knows after one automatic compaction of a 100K+ token synthetic session?
privacy: Metadata only: counts, codes, booleans, times, and hashes. No message text, request body, or key.

arms.plugin: context.engine warm_compaction: the plugin of this repository, installed with the Hermes install command and enabled. Default plugin settings.
arms.lcm: context.engine lcm: hermes-lcm 0.21.0-rc2 (Git commit 10cbb78347ec86f3004153b24767324ded9e37b4, the copy installed on the user's Hermes), copied into the session home as plugins/hermes-lcm and enabled. lcm.context_threshold 0.7 as in the user's config; every other LCM setting at its default (fresh tail 32 messages, leaf chunk 20,000 tokens, condensation fan-in 4, depth 3). The agent has the lcm_* recall tools (toolset context_engine).
arms.stock: context.engine compressor: the built-in compressor with its default settings.

protocol.fixture: fixture.py: ten synthetic operations sessions (ops01 to ops10), 64 exchanges each plus a seed exchange, about 104,500 DGX prompt tokens at the seed request. Six facts sit in exchanges 1 to 41, which all three engines move out of the verbatim history: the staging bucket, the batch size (changed once; the latest value is correct), the rollback snapshot, the maintenance window, the checksum ticket, and the read replica (in the middle of a long job log row). One control fact (the on-call contact) is in exchange 63. A standing rule in exchange 1 asks for an owner field in every JSON reply. The state in exchange 41 sets the next action: request_approval (4 cases), rerun_checksum (3 cases), or run_cutover (3 cases).

modes.auto: Seed turn. Then the runner sets threshold_tokens to auto_threshold_tokens and threshold_percent to auto_threshold_tokens / context_length on the engine instance of the agent. The continuation turn then compacts in the Hermes turn-start preflight before its first request. Then the probe turn. The user's settings do not start a compaction in the seed turn: plugin 0.50, LCM 0.70, built-in 0.50 of a 262,144-token window, against a seed prompt of about 104,500 tokens.

protocol.order: One worker process per case and arm, sequential, concurrency 1. The arm order rotates by case index: plugin-lcm-stock, lcm-stock-plugin, stock-plugin-lcm, and again.

measures.time: Host wall time in the worker. Compaction: the _compress_context calls inside the continuation turn. Continuation: the continuation turn minus the compaction. Workflow = compaction + continuation. Probe: the probe turn, including LCM tool calls.
measures.requests: Per HTTP request, metadata only: kind (main, warm, aux = built-in summary, lcm = LCM summary, fallback, aux_other, other), times, status, prompt, completion and cached tokens, finish reason, message count, and the SHA-256 of the messages.
measures.quality: fixture.score_continuation (action, target, approval_required, owner rule) and fixture.score_probe (six compacted facts, one control fact, owner rule), exact values after case and space folding.
measures.lcm_state: Row counts of the LCM tables and the depth and level columns of its summary nodes, read only from lcm.db after the session.

stop_rules: A worker that exits non-zero, times out (1800 s), writes no result, or fails a step check stops the run.
Step checks: the continuation turn makes at least one compaction; the continuation returns a reply.
Seed setup check as in plugin-live-03: a seed turn that does not end normally is a recorded setup failure, not a stop.
The seed request of the first session must report 90,000 to 125,000 prompt tokens, else the run stops.
A plugin path other than warm, an LCM summary fallback (L2 or L3), or a wrong answer is a measured result, not a stop.
protocol.engine_reason: The main request settings are those of plugin-live-02 (reasoning effort high, seed 7, draft on). The user's agent setting is reasoning_effort max; its mapping on this route was not checked, so the validated high setting is used.

host.summary_route_reason: As the user's config: auxiliary.compression on the DGX model with reasoning_effort none and a 600-second timeout. The built-in summary, the LCM summaries, lcm_expand_query, and the plugin fallback use this route. The plugin warm request uses the main request settings.

decision_rules.quality_facts: Per arm: correct compacted facts out of 60 (10 cases x 6). Report each fact, the superseded batch size, and the middle-of-row read replica separately. Arm A keeps more facts than arm B when its total is higher and it is higher in more cases than it is lower.
decision_rules.next_action: Per arm: next-action passes out of 10.
decision_rules.owner_rule: Per arm: owner field present and correct in the continuation reply and in the probe reply (out of 10 each).
decision_rules.control: The on-call contact is in the verbatim rows of every arm. Fewer than 9 of 10 correct in an arm marks a reply problem, not a compaction effect.
decision_rules.speed: For plugin against LCM and plugin against built-in: an arm is faster when its median is lower over the paired cases and it is lower in at least round(0.7 x n) of the n paired cases. Report the compaction alone, the workflow, and the probe turn.
decision_rules.cost: Report the model requests, prompt tokens, and completion tokens of each compaction.

observations: The next-action expectation of the three run_cutover cases has approval_required true, but the approval is already given in the session. All three arms answered false in two of these cases. Counted on action and target only, next-action passes are plugin 9/10, LCM 9/10, built-in 10/10. No next-action difference is claimed.

LCM cuts each message longer than 3,000 characters to its first 2,000 and last 800 characters before it summarizes. The read replica fact is in the middle of such a row: LCM 0/10, built-in 0/10, plugin 10/10.

After the in-place compaction, the LCM store held each message about twice (lcm_store). The summary node covers the first ingest only (99 messages), so the measured compaction is not affected. Recall tool results can contain duplicate rows.

The DGX prefix cache held the seed prompt of the arm that ran before the plugin arm of the same case, so most plugin seed turns were short. The seed turn is not a measure of any decision rule; the warm request reuses the seed request of its own session in every case.
limits: One synthetic task family, one session shape (text rows, no tool rows in the seeded history), one engine, and the user's settings for LCM and the summary route.

Facts other than the read replica sit at the start of a row. LCM and the built-in compressor cut long rows before they summarize; this placement favors them, and the read replica tests the opposite case.
The fence blocks the tiktoken download, so LCM counts tokens with its characters / 4 estimate in every session.
LCM appends its recall policy (about 2.2 KB) to each user message; this is LCM behavior and part of its arm.
Results describe these versions and settings only. They do not prove M0, M3, deployed compatibility, or other models.
